references.text: Herod had heard about Jesus and was perplexed as to who he was. Already here it is mentioned that Herod wanted to see Jesus: 'He tried to see him' ([ref:Luk 9:7-9|Luke 9:7-9]). This is the direct background for the joy Herod feels in 23:8.

Jesus refers to Herod as 'that fox' and shows that he is aware of Herod's interest and hostility ([ref:Luk 13:31-32|Luke 13:31-32]). This highlights the tension between Jesus and Herod, which culminates in their meeting during the trial.

Matthew also tells about Herod's knowledge of Jesus and his miracles ([ref:Matt 14:1-2|Matthew 14:1-2]). Herod heard what Jesus was doing, which corresponds to him having heard much about him in Luke 23:8.

Mark's parallel regarding Herod's knowledge of Jesus: Herod had heard about him, for Jesus' name had become known ([ref:Mark 6:14-16|Mark 6:14-16]). This supports the statement 'because he had heard about him' in Luke 23:8.

Jesus rebukes those who will not believe unless they see signs and wonders: 'If you do not see signs and wonders, you will not believe' ([ref:Joh 4:48|John 4:48]). Herod's desire to see a sign from Jesus illustrates exactly this attitude.

Jesus rejects the demand for a sign from 'an evil and adulterous generation' ([ref:Matt 12:38-39|Matthew 12:38-39]). Herod's hope to see a sign reflects the same sign-seeking attitude that Jesus repeatedly condemns.
Some demanded a sign from heaven from Jesus in order to test him ([ref:Luk 11:16|Luke 11:16]). Herod's expectation of seeing a sign stands within this same tradition of seeking signs.
The Pharisees demanded a sign from heaven, and Jesus sighed deeply and refused to give them any sign ([ref:Mark 8:11-12|Mark 8:11-12]). Herod received no sign either – Jesus did not answer him.
Paul writes that 'Jews demand signs' ([ref:1 Kor 1:22|1 Corinthians 1:22]). Herod's desire to see a sign from Jesus is an expression of this attitude of demanding visible proof rather than believing.

The immediate continuation: Herod asked Jesus many questions, but Jesus did not answer him, and Herod with his soldiers mocked him ([ref:Luk 23:9-11|Luke 23:9-11]). Herod's curiosity and sign-seeking were met with Jesus' silence.
